key_insight: LongMedBench evaluates medical AI agents on long-horizon clinical decisions by using real EHR timelines rather than short, isolated questions.
clinical_relevance: It better reflects how clinicians build decisions across repeated visits, tests, and evolving treatments, which may make agent evaluation more realistic.
method: Built from MIMIC-IV admission records and clinical notes
Converts records into time-series event streams and long-context memory datasets
Evaluates agents with three suites: fact-based QA, temporal reasoning, and long-horizon decision-making
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 335 patients, averaging 19.72 inpatient visits and 44.91 medical events per visit, and tests whether models can use explicit timestamps and long-range patient history.
watch_item: Performance may depend heavily on the model’s immediate context, so results may not fully capture robustness over extended real-world clinical workflows.
paper_title: LongMedBench: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Long-Horizon Clinical Decision-Making
